title: Credible deviations from signaling equilibria
summary_en: In standard signalling models, deviations from equilibrium are 'punished' by off-path beliefs that may not be credible. Eső and Schummer apply credibility refinements to signalling games and identify which deviations survive belief restrictions that require beliefs to be best-responses to plausible play. The paper sharpens the equilibrium-selection toolkit for signalling games and yields predictions that depart from the standard Spence-style benchmark in identifiable ways.
data_used: Theoretical paper in non-cooperative game theory. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Background theoretical input for any policy analysis based on signalling models — labour-market signalling, financial disclosure, advertising. The paper informs the equilibrium-selection assumptions made when assessing policies (e.g., disclosure mandates, certification schemes) that work through signalling channels.
